title: Evolution of Magnetism in Ce$_4$Ge$_7$ under Magnetic Field and Pressure
authors: Kaixin Ye, Qihe Yu, Yongjian Li, Yanan Zhang, Ye Chen, Rui Li, Lin Jiao, M. Smidman, Yongjun Zhang, Yu Liu, Huiqiu Yuan
abstract: We report the magnetic and transport properties of single-crystalline Ce$_4$Ge$_7$, which crystallizes in a non-centrosymmetric orthorhombic structure (space group C222$_1$). It undergoes an antiferromagnetic transition at $T_N$ = 7.3 K. When a magnetic field is applied along the $b$-axis, a metamagnetic transition occurs at 1.3 T (at 2 K). Correspondingly, this transition gives rise to an anomalous Hall effect, which is dominated by the intrinsic Karplus-Luttinger mechanism. Under hydrostatic pressure, $T_N$ of Ce$_4$Ge$_7$ initially increases slightly and is then gradually suppressed. For pressures above $P_c$ = 10.2 GPa, no magnetic order is observed. The divergence of the $A$ coefficient, the maximum of the residual resistivity, and the non-Fermi liquid behavior around $P_c$ indicate the possible existence of an antiferromagnetic quantum critical point in Ce$_4$Ge$_7$.
summary: This paper reports comprehensive measurements on Ce4Ge7, a heavy-fermion material, detailing its magnetic and electronic response to magnetic fields and pressure. Key findings include an antiferromagnetic transition, a field-induced metamagnetic transition, and strong evidence pointing towards an antiferromagnetic quantum critical point at a specific pressure. The work utilizes advanced transport diagnostics like the anomalous Hall effect to probe the underlying correlated electronic states.
main_problem: The study investigates the magnetic and transport properties of the heavy-fermion material Ce4Ge7 under external tuning parameters, specifically applied magnetic fields and hydrostatic pressure.
main_result: The material exhibits an antiferromagnetic transition, a field-induced metamagnetic transition accompanied by an anomalous Hall effect, and shows signatures of an antiferromagnetic quantum critical point near 10.2 GPa.
method: The research combines single-crystal synthesis, structural characterization (XRD), and advanced transport measurements, including magnetization, specific heat, resistivity, and anomalous Hall effect measurements under high pressure using a diamond anvil cell.
model_or_system: The system is single-crystalline Ce4Ge7, an orthorhombic heavy-fermion compound. The physics is analyzed using models for antiferromagnetic spin-wave excitations, Fermi liquid theory, and the intrinsic Karplus-Luttinger mechanism for the anomalous Hall effect.
key_observables: Antiferromagnetic transition temperature (TN), metamagnetic transition field, anomalous Hall conductivity (sigma_Axy), residual resistivity (rho_0), and the coefficient A in the temperature-dependent resistivity.
important_parameters: Magnetic field (up to 1.3 T), pressure (up to 24.3 GPa), and the critical pressure P_c = 10.2 GPa.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the anomalous Hall effect is dominated by the intrinsic Karplus-Luttinger mechanism, and that the low-temperature resistivity can be described by Fermi liquid or spin-wave models.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of resistivity and magnetic susceptibility with temperature and pressure, showing the AFM transition, the metamagnetic jump, and the divergence of transport coefficients near the critical pressure.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents measurements of magnetic and transport properties across varying fields and pressures. It first establishes the magnetic ground state (AFM transition), then analyzes the field-induced transitions (metamagnetism/AHE), and finally maps the phase diagram by studying the pressure dependence of the magnetic order and transport coefficients to locate the QCP.
why_interesting: The investigation of quantum critical points in heavy-fermion systems using pressure tuning is a canonical problem in condensed matter physics, providing experimental benchmarks for theories of quantum phase transitions and strongly correlated electron behavior.
